advances.name: Bombards
advances.desc: Great bronze guns that knock down in a week walls that held for a century.

advances.name: Pike and Shot
advances.desc: Squares of pikemen with handgunners on their flanks: infantry that stands against knights.

advances.name: Musket and Volley
advances.desc: Ranks of musketeers firing in turn, behind low star forts that shrug off cannon fire.

advances.name: Flintlock and Bayonet
advances.desc: Drilled soldiers whose every musket is also a pike: the last pikemen leave the battlefield.

advances.name: Caravels
advances.desc: Light, handy ships that beat back against the wind, so captains dare to follow the African coast south.

advances.name: Ocean Navigation
advances.desc: The astrolabe, tables of the sun and the trade winds: captains who can find their way home from the open ocean.

advances.name: Galleons
advances.desc: Tall, heavily gunned ships and charts drawn to scale: fleets that cross any ocean and settlers who arrive where they meant to.

advances.name: Ships of the Line
advances.desc: Battle fleets that fight in a single line, and trading companies that send them to every sea.

advances.name: The Printing Press
advances.desc: Movable type turns out more books in a week than a monastery of scribes copies in a year.

advances.name: Banking
advances.desc: Double-entry books, bills of exchange and great family banks: money moves across Europe without a coin changing hands.

advances.name: Statecraft
advances.desc: Secretaries schooled in Latin and law draft treaties, run chanceries and win over conquered towns.

advances.name: Royal Bureaucracy
advances.desc: Salaried officials, written records and learned academies, all answering to the crown.
